text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the median realised 20-session return was 2.96%, with a mean of 2.39%. The distribution is slightly left-skewed at -0.288, meaning the downside tail is thicker than the upside. The single number to anchor on is the 10th percentile: in 10% of these analogs, the name lost 8.68% or more over the next trading month.

[state]
The engine pulled these specific episodes because the current state combines several distinctive features. TSLA sits 26.98% below its 52-week high (z-score -0.841) and has drawn down 14.35% from its 60-session peak (z-score -0.749). Its 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 48.97% (z-score 0.983), yet the 5d/20d volatility ratio has collapsed to 0.489 (z-score -1.217), indicating a sudden compression in short-term variance against a volatile backdrop. Dollar volume is thin, with a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score of -1.558 (z-score -1.026). Macro context matters here too: WTI crude surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), while benchmark 20-session volatility remains low at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). The feature weights allocate 30% to name-level price/vol dynamics, 20% to market, 20% to macro, 10% to crypto, and 20% to event timing, with 45 calendar days to the next earnings release (z-score 0.663). This mix pulls in names across sectors rather than just other Consumer Disc. prints.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs spanning 2016-12-14 to 2026-08-17, the forward returns range from -11.47% to 15.49%, with a standard deviation of 6.9%. The distribution leans positive: 68% of the analogs finished above zero, while 32% finished below. The 25th percentile is -1.25% and the 75th percentile is 6.87%. The bad tail is dominated by a few specific sessions. Li Auto ADR (LI) on 2025-09-22 returned -11.47%, which is the worst outcome in the set. Boeing (BA) on 2021-08-04 returned -3.76%. On the upside, Schlumberger (SLB) on 2026-08-04 returned 12.48%, and Nike (NKE) on 2023-10-10 returned 12.03%. The closest match by distance is Thermo Fisher (TMO) on 2025-08-07 at 0.4262, which returned 8.33%. The only TSLA analog retrieved is TSLA itself on 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4374), which returned 8.87%. The retrieval spans 39 distinct sessions and 30 distinct symbols, heavily weighted toward Technology (12) and China ADR (7) names.

[tails]
Endpoint returns hide the path risk that makes a position un-holdable. In these 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -3.53%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -10.99%, and the 25th percentile was -7.38%. Looking at drawdown breaches during the 20-session horizon: 40% of the analogs breached a 5% drawdown at some point, and 14% breached a 10% drawdown. None breached 15% or 20%. Conversely, the median maximum favourable excursion was 6.73%, reaching 14.07% at the 90th percentile. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 1.91. The conformal interval, scaled at 1.768 around the median, runs from -9.24% to 15.15%, giving a total width of 24.38%.

[stress]
Three stress windows materially worsen the baseline picture. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario yields a median forward return of -7.83%, which is 10.79% worse than the baseline median (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -10.79), with a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: this nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produces a median return of -6.29%, 9.25% worse than baseline (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -9.25), with a 50% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash shows a median return of -3.2%, with a deltaMedianVsBaselinePct of -6.16, and a 72.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. Among shock scenarios, the earnings release day stands out with a median return of -1.18% (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -4.14) and a 48% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) gives a median of -2.28% (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -5.24); caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket scenario yields a median of 0.13% (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -2.83) but a 34% probability of a 10% drawdown; caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, and when measured on the wrapper itself (TSLAG_USDT), 47.37% of realised hourly movement happened while the reference market was closed. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind shows a median of -0.03% (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -2.99) with a 44.4% breach probability; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock gives a median of -0.86% (deltaMedianVsBaselinePct -3.82); caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The FOMC decision day scenario was not skipped and shows a median of 1.7%; caveat: only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Out-of-sample coverage is 87.4% against an 80% target, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -3.4%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter. The PIT chi-square statistic is 363.9 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the failure of uniformity. The directional hit rate is only 54%. The dataset relies on api.stockanalysis.com for prices and SEC full-text search for earnings, which introduces noise.

Regarding the instrument you would actually trade: the wrapper status is "measured" for TSLAG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4. It is classified as a "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9561 and a tracking error of 100 bp/day. The premium band over the underlying's last raw close of 364.27 ranges from -0.43% (p10) to 0.41% (p90), with a price deviation of 4.88% and a last wrapper print of 382.05. The spread is 17.82 bps. Crucially, the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 47.37% of the wrapper's own realised hourly price movement occurred during those closed hours. The wrapper's caveat notes that it is measured on Gate.io spot v4, not the official Bitget MCP, and that a fair tracker carries its own idiosyncratic risk at 100 bp/day of tracking error.

For the return layer that can actually be sized: across 4 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend block return was -0.094%, the 10th percentile was -1.2906%, and the standard deviation was 1.278%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.521%. Zero percent of these specific weekend blocks breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
